title: RAW UNREVIEWED: contested kinship reuses one return-status claim across a change of addressee
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Luke15.11–32 motivates a complete reconciliation narrative with three principal family members. The same returning person is described as the speaker's son and the addressee's brother while a repeated condition claim persists. A claim of unworthiness is distinct from erasing kinship. This imposes reference, relation and assertion-scope consequences beyond a tense/status list. No words or source copying are identified.

design.author_role: bounded independent idea producer; root owns scientific selection
design.whole_content_hypothesis: A reconciliation narrative retains one family graph through departure, proposed degradation, welcome and contested inclusion. The repetition is a reason offered to different audiences, with a relational subject expression changing with speaker/addressee. It does not consist of a sequence of individually named stages or a generic success/failure machine.

source.historical_limit: The canonical parable supplies historically intelligible content. These English access witnesses supply no Voynich date, locality, exemplar, original language or direct source-dependence claim. No default Latin writer is assumed.
source.complete_source_synopsis: A father has two sons. The younger takes his share, spends it, suffers hunger and returns after planning to request servant treatment. He declares himself unworthy of sonship; the father welcomes him and celebrates. The elder objects. The father addresses the elder as son, identifies the returned younger as his brother, and repeats the earlier dead/alive and lost/found reason for celebration.
source.textual_limits: The servant-treatment request occurs in the planned speech but is not included in the reported speech of verse21 in these witnesses. Unworthiness is asserted by the returning speaker; the narrator continues calling him son. Do not insert actual disowning, literal bodily resurrection, a second inheritance distribution, an elder's agreement, or a completed reconciliation that the ending does not state.

proposed_global_reading_contract.participants: F is father; Y and E are distinct younger/elder sons. These are analyst variables, not three newly coined target names or three whole-form glosses. A written introduction and distinguishing references must identify them. For the minimal closed model the principal family roster is exactly F,Y,E; extending that roster costs an explicit additional participant, not an invisible repair.
proposed_global_reading_contract.shared_relations: One CHILD(parent,child) relation gives CHILD(F,Y) and CHILD(F,E). BROTHER(E,Y) is separately expressed or derived by an explicitly declared same-parent/distinct-child rule. No generation edge is exported to other f83r records. MY resolves to the current speaker; YOUR resolves to the current addressee. A speech constructor must provide those owners, rather than the paragraph boundary supplying them silently.
proposed_global_reading_contract.reused_condition: One composed condition package K refers to Y and is asserted twice by F in different address frames. K contains the same opposed earlier/current predications both times; it is not a distinct word value for each occurrence. Its two source condition pairs must remain separate or an explicitly paid synonym/equivalence rule must relate them. Neither pair requires a physical death/revival interpretation. The final address supplies the later consumer: F offers the repeated condition with the brother relation as the reason for celebration to the refusing E. It does not assert E subsequently enters or agrees.
proposed_global_reading_contract.scope: A speaker's denial of worthiness-to-be-called-child does not negate CHILD(F,Y) in the narrator/father frame. A planned request does not automatically become an executed social reclassification. Quotation, intended speech, actual speech and narrator assertion must use globally fixed scope rules if distinguished.
proposed_global_reading_contract.full_account_debt: A future whole P1 author must account for every group and reader alternative, including introduction, property division, departure, spending, hunger/employment, planned and actual speech, welcome and celebration, the elder's objection, and the father's unfinished invitation. This RAW supplies no 72-group translation, spatial allocation, segmentation, vocabulary table or line-to-verse mapping. A short shared condition cannot be substituted for the entire narrative.

two_step_discriminating_consequences.steps: Bind the two CHILD edges and distinguish F,Y,E; then resolve the first condition's relational subject as CHILD(MY,Y) in F's speech and the final subject as BROTHER(YOUR,Y) in F's address to E.
two_step_discriminating_consequences.outcome: Both composed condition packages must concern the same Y, although their subject descriptions and address frame differ. The later invitation/reason is addressed to E about his brother Y, not to Y about himself or to F about F's brother. If the final YOUR instead resolves to F or Y, the selected complete family graph yields a different or self relation and changes whose family relationship supports that invitation. A global fixed-person interpretation of YOUR cannot preserve all speech turns. Actual participation by E remains unstated.
two_step_discriminating_consequences.changed_research_decision: A whole account with an actual shared reference construction surviving both frames would retain this relational narrative as a C0 candidate. An account needing occurrence-specific identities or whole-sentence terminal values would be stopped before more lexical authoring. No independent meaning confirmation follows.

two_step_discriminating_consequences.steps: Keep the returning speaker's unworthiness claim within its declared speech scope; then evaluate the father's subsequent CHILD assertion and the elder-addressed BROTHER expression against the unchanged family graph.
two_step_discriminating_consequences.outcome: The narrative can contain a sincere unworthiness claim and continuing kinship without a world-level contradiction. A rival that turns the first claim into deletion of the child relation must explicitly restore it before the later brother statement; that restoration is an extra written proposition, not an invisible repair.
two_step_discriminating_consequences.changed_research_decision: If a frozen grammar collapses quoted eligibility and narrator relation into one global status bit, it fails this paid narrative contract. If the distinction is written and recurrent, preserve it as semantic-scope capacity, with all literal labels unconfirmed.

rivals_and_equivalences.difference: Repeated condition terms are attached to separately introduced examples; no shared person or audience-relative relation is required. A written shared reference across the complete narrative, rather than two guessed status labels, is needed to distinguish it.

rivals_and_equivalences.name: world-level disowning followed by reinstatement
rivals_and_equivalences.difference: The child relation is genuinely removed, then reinstated. It can match the later relation if an additional restoration is written; the source narrative alone does not license supplying that step silently.

rivals_and_equivalences.name: fixed-owner possessive
rivals_and_equivalences.difference: MY/YOUR refer to one global owner instead of speaker/addressee. It changes a relational argument under the selected three-person frame; a different legitimate nondeictic grammar remains possible until actual target frames are authored.

rivals_and_equivalences.difference: A nonbiblical account may realize the identical family/reference graph and condition reuse. This equivalence is retained: passing a C0 conformance check would not identify Luke, religion, literal kinship, an original language or the true meanings.

design.stopping_rule: Stop this fixed account if its unchanged pronoun/scope grammar changes the returning person's identity, turns his unworthiness speech into an unexpressed world-level disowning, or supplies an invisible restoration/extra sibling to avoid a conflict. Also stop if the only semantic consequence is an author-supplied Y=Y identity with no later reused written relation. Missing independent meaning confirmation alone does not erase this RAW.
